Chapter 8: Designing With Intention—Creating Habits and Environments That Support Change.
You know, big dreams aren’t made overnight. They’re built on those small, everyday choices that most of us barely notice. The funny thing is, so many people underestimate just how much habits and our environments shape who we become. We like to think it’s all about sheer willpower—but honestly, that’s rarely enough to make changes stick. What really works? Intentionally designing your routines, your spaces, and even your relationships to set yourself up for growth.
Picture this: there’s a man who always dreamed of writing a novel. For years, he told himself he was just too busy. But deep down, he knew distractions were his real enemy. So, he decided to shake things up. He set his alarm for thirty minutes earlier, and—here’s the bold move—left his phone in another room. The first few mornings were tough, sure. But soon, that quiet time became a little sanctuary. The words started flowing, not because he suddenly had more willpower, but because he’d made it easier to focus on what really mattered.
Or think of the woman who wanted to eat healthier, but always found herself grabbing snacks in the afternoon. She realized her kitchen was full of temptations, and stress made her reach for food almost without thinking. So instead of trying to muscle through with willpower, she got a bit strategic. She prepped healthy snacks ahead of time and put them right where she’d see them. Then, she started a new ritual—making tea and sitting by the window, instead of snacking at her desk. The changes were subtle, but they added up, bit by bit.
It’s wild how much our environment shapes what we do, often without us even realizing it. A cluttered workspace can drain your motivation. But a supportive friend? That can be a game changer. Take the person who struggled to exercise, until they joined a walking group. Suddenly, the accountability and camaraderie made it easier to show up—even on those days when motivation was nowhere to be found.
Habits are the true building blocks of change. They’re shaped by repetition, sure, but also by intention. Like the young parent, totally overwhelmed by the chaos of family life. She started a bedtime ritual with her kids—reading together, sharing gratitude, and switching off screens. That routine didn’t just bring calm; it became an anchor, something comforting to return to when life felt stressful.
Here’s something to pay attention to: most people try to change way too much at once, and then feel discouraged when it doesn’t work out. Real change? It’s all about small, consistent actions. Making the behavior you want the easiest choice—and removing the stuff that gets in your way.
And don’t forget, designing with intention also means being gentle with yourself when things don’t go as planned. Like the man who wanted to meditate every day, but missed a few sessions. Instead of giving up, he reminded himself that progress isn’t always a straight line. He tweaked his routine, found a better time, and simply kept going.
So, if you want to create lasting change, start by designing your habits and your surroundings with intention. Make it easier to do what matters. Give yourself permission to experiment, adjust, and keep moving forward—even if it’s just one small step at a time.
